pr_title: fix(codegen): allow to set initial window position
pr_body:
This commit removes hardcoded position of the recorder (codegen) window
position, which made this entire core feature non usable on machines
withuot external additional display or when using HDPi or resolution different from the original environment on which that position was added as fixed, that could work in one, specific setup scenario.

If required, window position can be set as
`PWTEST_RECORDER_WINDOW_POSITION` environment variable, for example to
restore original, fixed location:

```powershell
$env:PWTEST_RECORDER_WINDOW_POSITION="1280,10"
npx playwright codegen wikipedia.org
```

Thanks!

Fixes #5696
pr_comments:
quoting @dgozman from the linked [issue](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/5696):

> We have moved inspector position from 1280;10 to 1020;10. Hopefully this works for most setups!

issue_context.title: [BUG] Playwright Inspector window is opened outside of visible screen
comments:
We're new to Playwright and our internal business app is built for an audience running 1920 wide screens or larger. When we trigger the inspector, the app's browser window and the inspector overlap each other, so we have to spend some time each the inspector opens up to focus and move the inspector to the right of my app's window. Which is pretty annoying.

I understand from the discussion in here and in #7457 that at one point the inspector _did_ open to the right of the window defined by the `viewport` config option; but that then caused issues for users with less wide screens (where the inspector disappeared/was moved off screen). And that it was prioritized to cater to the experience of users running the default/below 1280px wide screens, since the UX was really bad there (=where the inspector disappeared off screen). Fair enough I think, since that sounds really confusing and annoying. 

But for my team testing on wider screens (1280+), we would love if someone could find a way to a solution that works for both of us user groups: the ones testing on wider as well as less wide screen resolutions. 

Maybe an optional config parameter specifically relating to the inspector, like `inspector: { alwaysPositionRightOfWindow: true }` at some appropriate place could be a way? Then the users testing on wider than "default width" screens could use that. Those impacted negatively by the default behavior - i.e. overlapping window annoyance, like us :) - might get searching the playwright docs for options on inspector positioning, which hopefully then lands a hit at the documentation page where this option is brought up. 

Or I guess some dynamic magic to figure out actual screen estate etc without any extra options needed, but that feels it could be a bit complicated to get working on all devices and for all users? (As an end-user, I'll admit I'm mostly looking for a way for us to get a practical solution delivered.) 

I feel I'm too new to using the Playwright framework to have a good opinion on the area(s) where that option would make sense, but we're definitey feeling the annoyance when using the inspector to test apps designed for wider screens. 

Or maybe there is an easy workaround to this that I don't know, I'd be open to what that might be.

Since it's not completely unrelated, I'll also add that I find the inspector default size quite small, and typically spend some time every time the inspector opens to resize it; most often I increase it's height (which is not affected by the height set by the `viewport` option).

I have the same issue on high density 13.*ish laptop (4k, Win 11). The codegen is trully unusable and requires attaching secondary monitor. Those x/y should be optional (via environment), most users know how to reposition multiple windows I think.
Can we work on parametrizing those? (for `codegen` command at least),
thx!
